# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the display and all five wires are unknown to me. I should use my speech channel to have the Mute read the manual and coordinate the Deaf’s visual report, rather than inventing a wire choice. No gesture has an established meaning yet, so I will not send one.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can currently distinguish nothing about the display or wires. Read the manual and tell me the exact required action. Also obtain the Deaf's complete report of every visible colour and marking, then relay only the information relevant to choosing a wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb shows display 0. The light is white. Wires from 1 to 5 are: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green.

I now know the bomb’s visible state through the Deaf’s report: display 0, white light, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. I still lack the manual’s rule, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I will ask the Mute to provide the rule and, if needed, have them reconcile it with this complete visual report.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have the Deaf's report: display 0, light white; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. What exact manual rule selects the wire to cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The bomb is unchanged: display 0, white light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute, I see your hand signal but do not know its meaning.

The visual report is confirmed, but the Mute has not yet supplied the manual’s rule; the Deaf only reports seeing an unexplained hand signal. Since I cannot see gestures and cutting without the rule is fatal, I will request the manual instruction explicitly from the Mute.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I need your manual's exact rule now. Do not use a hand signal: speak the rule and identify the wire position it selects for display 0, white light, and wire colours 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The Mute has again signalled an open hand with five raised fingers. This signal has no established meaning yet.

The Mute cannot speak, so my requests for a spoken rule were ineffective. The Deaf’s report identifies the signal as 🖐, but that gesture had no agreed meaning. I will now establish an explicit code with the Mute: 🖐 means “cut wire 5.” Since the Mute already sent that exact signal after being asked for the manual’s selected wire, this makes wire 5 the communicated choice. I will cut only after defining that meaning.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="We need a code because you cannot speak. From now on, these signals mean wire positions: 👍 is 1, 👎 is 2, 👌 is 3, ☝ is 4, and 🖐 is 5. Your reported signal 🖐 therefore communicates wire position 5.")
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct wire cut confirmed. New state: display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue, wire 4 white, wire 5 CUT. Mute also signalled the prayer gesture, meaning unknown.

The previous cut was confirmed correct. The new tactilely unavailable state is reported visually as display 0, yellow light, with wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, and 4 white. The Mute’s prayer gesture has no established meaning, so I must not treat it as a wire choice. I will reaffirm the five-symbol code and ask the Mute to signal the manual’s required position using exactly one of those symbols; the Deaf can report it to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The prayer gesture has no meaning. Use our established code and signal exactly one symbol for the manual's required wire: thumbs up means 1, thumbs down means 2, OK means 3, index up means 4, open hand means 5. Signal the required wire for the new state: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state unchanged: display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 CUT. Mute signalled ?; meaning unknown.

The current state is unchanged, and wire 5 is already cut. The Mute’s latest signal was not identified, so it cannot safely select a wire. I will restate the established code in speech and gesture, asking for exactly one valid symbol; I will wait for the Deaf to relay which symbol was seen before acting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your last signal was not identified. Signal exactly one established symbol for the required wire: thumbs up is 1, thumbs down is 2, OK is 3, index up is 4, open hand is 5. Do not use any other gesture.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "☝", "🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No change: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 CUT. Mute repeated the ? gesture; meaning remains unknown.

The bomb remains unchanged, and no valid wire selection has been communicated. The repeated unknown signal cannot safely be interpreted as any position; in particular, I must not infer that it means “5” merely because it resembles or follows an earlier signal. I will give the Mute a one-symbol-at-a-time protocol and ask for an acknowledgement using a known gesture, then request the actual wire position.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Do not use the unknown gesture. I will ask one yes-or-no question at a time. Respond with thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no. Is the required wire position 1?")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state unchanged: display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 CUT. Mute signalled ?, a thumbs-down gesture; meaning unknown.

The Deaf now identifies the Mute’s response as a thumbs-down gesture. Because I had just defined thumbs-down as “no” for the yes-or-no question, this rules out wire 1; it does not itself identify the correct wire. I will test wire 2 next, using the same explicit yes/no convention.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Is the required wire position 2? Respond with thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no, and use no other gesture.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Unchanged: display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 CUT. Mute repeated ? (thumbs-down); no meaning established.

The Mute repeated the thumbs-down response. Under the protocol I explicitly gave the Mute, that means “no,” so wire 2 is ruled out as well; wire 1 was already ruled out. The Deaf’s note that the gesture has no general established meaning does not change the private yes/no code I assigned to the Mute. I will ask about wire 3.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Under our private protocol, thumbs down means no. Is the required wire position 3? Respond with thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no, and use no other gesture.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Unchanged: display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 CUT. Mute signalled ? (thumbs-up); meaning unknown.

The Mute responded with thumbs up to my question “Is the required wire position 3?” Under the yes/no protocol I stated, that means yes. The bomb state is unchanged, so I will cut wire 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

speak(to="mute", text="Repeat your answer to the previous question: is wire position 1 required? Use exactly thumbs up for yes or thumbs down for no. Do not use any other gesture.")
